ConsentIn.description:
What the person read and ticked: the lines the server built for this offer (GET
/api/billing/consent/*, or the change preview's `consent`), sent back unchanged. The route
builds them again from the same facts and refuses any difference (409 consent_mismatch,
October 28, 2026), so what is kept is always the server's own text.
ConsentIn.title: ConsentIn

ConsentTextOut.description: What to show above the box, and exactly what to send back when it is ticked.
ConsentTextOut.title: ConsentTextOut

HelpedTotals.description: How many members answered and how many picked each choice: never who picked what.
HelpedTotals.title: HelpedTotals

NativeSubscriptionIn.description: An APNs or FCM device token from the native shell (chunk 2.3). Never money data.
NativeSubscriptionIn.title: NativeSubscriptionIn

NativeSyncIn.description: A purchase or restore from the shell (chunk 2.4): the store's own proof.
NativeSyncIn.title: NativeSyncIn

post.description: Soft delete now; the grace period and purge are `deletion.py`. The body must say DELETE.
A one-time code to the new address; the old one stays until it is verified.
Server-held data for the ZIP the device builds. Needs a fresh passkey check.

The app's screen locked (idle, or the person locked it): this session is locked on the
server too until the next passkey check (owner decision, October 28, 2026). Works on a
session that is already locked; not audited, like the idle lock it mirrors.

Sign in with a passkey the device already has (October 13, 2026): no email, no code.
The device shows its own picker of the passkeys it holds for this site.

A verified passkey (with Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint or device passcode) signs in and
unlocks in one step: it is the stronger of our two factors, and phishing-resistant. Same
audit and new-sign-in alert as an email-code sign-in.

get.description: The app's first call on start-up. Never an error: `authenticated` says it all.

The newest backup, or with `before` the newest one older than that backup: a device that
can't open a copy steps back to the one before it (October 24, 2026). A `before` copy that
is no longer kept (pruned while the device walked, after another upload) answers 409
`backup_gone`, never 404 `no_backup`, which means there is nothing (older) to restore; the
device then starts again from the newest (invariant 20, October 27, 2026).

post.description:
Switch plan or billing period now (owner decision, October 17, 2026). Up (Private →
Connected, or monthly → yearly) is charged the difference; down leaves the unused part as
credit, opens 30 days after the plan started or last changed, and disconnects linked banks
when the new plan doesn't link. Switching also undoes a cancellation.

What a switch costs before it happens: today's charge for an upgrade (the new price
less the unused part of the old), or the credit a downgrade leaves for the next bills.

get.description: The "If you cancel" lines for the plan that renews now, as /cancel will check them.
The "Before you subscribe" lines for one offer, as the checkout will check them.

Credit waiting on the account, and what deleting the account now would refund: the
months after the current one, at the price paid, plus the credit (shown before anyone
deletes).

schema.title: Response Get Entitlements Api Billing Entitlements Get

get.description:
Plan history (owner decision, October 18, 2026): what happened to the plan, newest
first.

schema.title: Response History Api Billing History Get

post.description:
Attach a store purchase to the signed-in account. No step-up here by design: the signed
transaction / verified token is stronger proof than a passkey check (the store already
authenticated the buyer, and a stolen session cannot fabricate one); the app still asks for
step-up before starting a purchase, like the web checkout.
Undo a cancellation before the period ends: renewal continues as before.

Tester tools (owner decision, October 18, 2026): an admin switches their own plan for
free, as often as they like, to test every plan; `plan: null` goes back to the real one.
Nothing is charged and Stripe is not involved. Anyone else gets 404, as if the route were
not there. Audited and alerted like any plan change.

Start the free trial the person picked (owner decision, October 14, 2026): once per
email, no card. Either plan runs 3 days (plans.yaml `trials`, since October 22, 2026).

schema.title: Response Start Trial Api Billing Trial Post
Response List Groups Api Groups Get

post.description: Start a challenge of the chosen type; the creator is its first member.
What a code points at, before joining. An unknown code is 404 like any other miss.
Owner only: the old code stops working at once.

put.description:
The member's own "What helped": up to 5 ids from the fixed list; [] clears it. Open once
they reached their target or the challenge ended (409 not_yet before).

delete.description: Owner only. Removing yourself is not leaving: use /leave.

put.description: The one number a device sends: percent of the member's own target. Never an amount.

schema.title: Response List Blobs Api Household Blobs Get

delete.description:
No step-up: leaving is never harder than joining (docs/security/linking.md). If the
provider can't be reached, the connection is hidden now and `stackd-api revoke-links`
keeps trying, so the user is never stuck with a connection they asked to drop.

post.description: Pass-through, like sync: the card facts go to the device and nowhere else.

Plaid update mode for a connection whose bank wants the user to sign in again. No
step-up: it restores what the user already allowed and reads nothing new.

Pass-through: the provider's changes go to the device and nowhere else. Nothing about
the transactions is logged or stored; the connection only notes when it was last read.
An APNs / FCM device token from the shell: stored encrypted, like a Web Push one.
One push saying notifications are on: proves the channel, carries nothing else.

get.description:
The last 30 days of sign-ins, failed sign-in attempts and security changes on this
account, newest first (at most 100), so a user can spot anything that was not them.

schema.title: Response Activity Api Security Activity Get

get.description:
Every device signed in now, then those whose session ended in the last 30 days, with
when and how it ended. No IP addresses: only keyed hashes are stored.

schema.title: Response List Devices Api Security Devices Get

put.description:
Auto-lock after this many idle minutes, on every device (owner decision, October 12,
2026). The server enforces it too: an idle session past it is locked for every request.

schema.title: Response List Passkeys Api Security Passkeys Get
